prompts.story-prompt.txt:
Edit target: the provided original Chinese diary sprite atlas. Produce the SAME 2048x2048 RGBA atlas with real transparent background. Preserve all four book-page sprites EXACTLY in their original locations, sizes, outlines, black covers, gold binding rings, perspective, burns, stains, torn and crumpled aged yellow parchment, and all transparent padding at the right. Do not rearrange, enlarge, straighten or crop any sprite. Replace ONLY the Chinese ink on the four page surfaces with the following exact English text, in dark charcoal legible hand-written journal lettering matching the original mood. Naturally reconstruct parchment behind old ink rather than painting flat rectangles. Keep a comfortable margin, fit text entirely inside each paper page. Preserve words exactly; line breaks can be adjusted only to fit. No headings, page numbers, decorations or added text. The names Sword-shroom and Shield-shroom are verified game terminology; preserve spelling.

TOP LEFT:
Sword and shield work in perfect harmony.
The shield holds the line and bears the onslaught;
the blade waits behind it for a chance to strike.
One defends, one advances. Each relies on the other.
I thought only we fought this way, but some plants
understand it just as well.
Yelena calls them Sword-shroom and Shield-shroom.
I would have called them the blade that breaks
the line and the shield that stands guard.
There is a strange bond between these mushrooms.
They share an origin, can fuse with each other,
and can change from one form to the other.
Alternating forms pushes their power to its limits.
I have to admit, they are impressive.
Fortunately, we are friends now.

TOP RIGHT:
We have reached the depths of the snowfield.
While travelling, I felt something strange underfoot.
Brushing aside the snow revealed some small
mushrooms hiding beneath it.
They seem quite fond of me. Had they not reached
out and wound their roots around me, we would
never have noticed them.
Later, we encountered some iron penguins.
Before we could act, those gentle mushrooms
struck first. Their sharp roots easily pierced
the metal shells.
Yelena was upset that she had not spotted the
mushrooms herself. I understand how she feels.
Had they been hostile, we would have paid
for that oversight today.

BOTTOM LEFT:
Our mission is to find and retrieve the source
of an unknown signal in this snowfield.
So far, it seems like a fuss over nothing.
Apart from the unexplained endless night,
there is only strange scrap metal all around.
We cannot make sense of this technology.
Luckily, Yelena can. She always knows everything.
I only care for flowers and plants.
Sadly, they rarely return the affection.
But the local plants surprised me today.
Perhaps they failed to notice I am a zombie,
and were happy to live alongside me.
Or perhaps, in a land that has lost the daylight,
even zombies seem a little less unwelcome.
I never would have imagined that one day,
we too would miss the sun.

BOTTOM RIGHT:
Yelena values every chance to keep our
teammates from getting hurt.
It took a good deal of persuasion to get the
squad to accept the plants travelling with us.
To be precise, everyone fell in love with
that green mushroom.
Who knew mushrooms understood swordplay?
With their help, we destroyed those machines
that glowed green.

Those big, rather dim-looking birds deserve
a mention, too. They seemed gentle and harmless,
until someone threw a snowball at one.
Their tails store sunlight. Could that mean
this snowfield was not always a place
of endless night?
